# Circulation of the blood (`blood_circulation`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/medicine.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Medicine & hygiene (`medicine`)
- Deps: helped by anatomy_dissection, piston_pump, microscope, measurement_quantification
- Core idea: The heart is a pump with valves. It drives the same blood round and round: out through the arteries to the body, back through the veins, then through the lungs and out again. Blood is not made afresh in the liver and used up in the flesh. Harvey's proof is arithmetic: if the heart throws out even a small mouthful at each beat, over a thousand beats in half an hour, it moves more blood in an hour than the whole body holds or any meal could supply. The demonstration: tie a band round the upper arm so the veins swell, then press along a vein. The little valves let blood pass only towards the heart. The fine vessels joining arteries to veins are too small to see without a microscope.
- Pitfalls:
  - Saying all arteries carry bright blood and all veins dark; the vessels between heart and lungs are the reverse
  - Claiming it changed medicine at once; bleeding went on for two more centuries
  - Crediting Harvey with knowing what the lungs do or seeing capillaries; he did neither
  - Calling older ideas stupid; Galen's ebb-and-flow system explained a great deal and Harvey kept much of it
- History: china: c. 2nd–1st c. BC – Huangdi neijing speaks of blood and qi flowing in an endless circuit; a doctrine, not an anatomical demonstration; islamic: c. 1242 – Ibn al-Nafis (Damascus, Cairo) denies the pores in the heart wall and describes blood passing through the lungs; europe: 1553 Servetus and 1559 Colombo describe the passage through the lungs; 1603 Fabricius describes the valves in veins; 1628 Harvey, De motu cordis; 1661 Malpighi sees capillaries in a frog's lung; 1733 Hales measures blood pressure in a horse
- Read:
  - William Harvey, Exercitatio anatomica de motu cordis et sanguinis in animalibus (1628)
  - Thomas Wright, Circulation: William Harvey's Revolutionary Idea (2012)
